To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stability of HIV RNA copy numbers in plasma is maintained under a wide variety of storage and handling conditions, and the HIV RNA copy numbers correlate well with the ability to isolate HIV by coculture with PBMCs.

the HIV RNA copy numbers in blood and plasma specimens remain stable for at least 3 days at room temperature or at 4°C and remain stable for at the least one freeze-thaw cycle, and that HIV RNA copy numbers correlate with the ability of PBMCs from the same specimens to support HIV isolation by coculture.
HIV RNA in blood or plasma samples can be stored at room temperature or at 4°C for at least 3 days and can be frozen and thawed once without affecting the RNA copy number.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of conditions encountered during handling, processing, and storage of plasma specimens on the quantity and quality of the human immunodeficiency RNA (HIV RNA).

the stability of HIV RNA in blood specimens under conditions that are likely to be encountered during routine clinical laboratory procedures and indicates that HIV RNA can be reliably measured in plasma specimens under these conditions.
the stability of the HIV RNA copy numbers in blood samples under a variety of conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV RNA is relatively stable in whole blood and plasma, and the Amplicor assay provides a useful method for measuring the HIV RNA copy numbers in plasma.
HIV RNA in plasma can be stored for at least 3 days at room temperature or at 4°C and that plasma can be frozen and stored at −70°C for at least 1 year without loss of HIV RNA.
the stability of HIV RNA in blood specimens is excellent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV RNA copy numbers are relatively stable under a variety of conditions often encountered in the handling and storage of blood samples.
the HIV RNA copy numbers measured by PCR-based assays are stable under the conditions examined.

, under most circumstances, the HIV RNA copy numbers measured by the Amplicor HIV RNA PCR assay are maintained in the presence of conditions that may be encountered during the handling and processing of blood and/or plasma samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with proper care, HIV RNA copy numbers can be accurately measured in blood specimens that have been held for up to 72 h at room temperature or refrigerated at 4°C.
HIV RNA copy numbers in blood and plasma are stable for at least 3 days at room temperature and 4°C and are stable with limited freezing and thawing.

the HIV RNA copy numbers measured with a commercial PCR-based assay are stable for at least 3 days at room temperature or at 4°C and are stable after freezing and thawing or long-term storage at −70°C, provided that the plasma is not contaminated with hemoglobin.
